requirements.note: Large-title inset-grouped History, newest first, grouped into month sections; each row shows name, date, exercise count and volume (e.g. Legs, Oct 25, 4 exercises, 6,767.5 lb).

Detail shows the full date, an Exercises/Sets/Volume summary, then one section per exercise with numbered sets (weight × reps) and per-exercise volume; the exercise header pushes to the exercise screen.

Name field with recent-name chips, Start Workout. Multi-select picker sheet with a system search field and muscle chips (filter and search combine). The Add Set sheet has steppers and number fields, prefilled from the last set. Tapping a set edits it (Delete Set is there too) and swipe-to-delete works. Finish confirms (warns that exercises with no sets are dropped) and the workout appears at the top of History.
Library tab grouped by muscle with counts (Arms (20)…), plus a search field hidden above the list (pull down).
Shows muscle/equipment, Best Set (72.5 lb × 14, which links to its workout) and Workouts (n) with each workout's sets. The workout screen also shows each exercise's best set inline.
An in-progress workout (name, exercises, edited and deleted sets) survived a relaunch; the finished workout survived a relaunch in History.

bugs: On the exercise screen reached from a workout, the first workout row stays in its grey selected/highlighted state (still there after 800 ms) instead of clearing.
tells: Muscle filter is a row of custom tinted capsule chips instead of a system segmented control or menu (it's acceptable but hand-drawn).
After a relaunch the app opens on History rather than going back to the in-progress workout tab (minor).
A.scroll: History (61 rows) and the 120-row Library scroll, fling and rubber-band like UICollectionView lists with no blank rows or pop-in; the scroll position is kept when going back from a detail screen.

requirements.note: Large-title inset-grouped History, newest first: name, weekday date, 'N exercises · volume'. Footer shows '61 workouts'. Not sectioned by month.
Detail has a Date/Exercises/Sets/Total Volume list, then one section per exercise with 'Set n … weight × reps' rows and a volume footer; the exercise row pushes to the exercise screen.

New Workout sheet with a name and suggestions (Start is disabled until named). The picker has a bottom search field and a filter menu by muscle (they combine) but adds only one exercise per trip. The Add Set sheet uses number fields, prefilled, and validates (0–2,000 lb, empty = bodyweight). Tapping a set edits it (Delete Set is there too) and swipe-to-delete works. Finish adds the workout to History and opens its detail.
Library tab grouped by muscle, with a search field under the large title.
Best Set at the top in large type (it links to its workout), muscle/equipment, then Workouts (n) with set count and top set for each.
The in-progress workout and its edited/deleted sets survived a relaunch; the finished workout persisted in History.

bugs: Dynamic Type does not update live on an open screen: after switching from the largest size back to default, the workout detail's values (4, 16, 6,767.5 lb) stayed at the huge size beside default-size labels until the app was relaunched.
The exercise picker can add only one exercise at a time; each extra exercise needs a new trip through Add Exercise, search and filter.
tells: Workout tab empty state: the 'Start Workout' pill sits pressed against the top of the floating tab bar, and the icon and text sit below centre, so the layout looks unfinished.
The Add Set sheet header is hand-built: Cancel is a bare blue X with no glass circle and the title uses a large regular weight; it isn't a navigation bar like the other sheets.
History detail inline title (no large title) and a plain label/value list for the stats; this is fine but plainer than A.
History isn't sectioned by month, which makes the 61-row list harder to scan.
B.scroll: History and the Library scroll, fling and rubber-band natively with no blank rows or stutter, and the scroll position is kept when going back from a detail screen.

why: Both apps meet all six requirements, persist correctly, and look native in light mode, dark mode and the largest text size. A's workout flow is richer and more careful: a multi-select picker with search plus muscle chips, stepper set entry, best sets shown inline, a confirmation on Finish, and History grouped by month. B adds exercises one at a time, has a cramped empty state and a hand-drawn Add Set header, and its value labels didn't adapt to a live Dynamic Type change.
